newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - Czech cenbank boosts battle to bolster crown.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Czech cenbank boosts battle to bolster crown.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) intensified its battle to shore up the weary crown on Wednesday, imposing further limits on banks' access to the last resort lending facility, the Lombard rate.

After imposing a limit to Lombard access of an unspecified portion of a bank's capital on Tuesday, the CNB told Reuters on Wednesday that access had been cut even more, and that the CNB was prepared to intervene further through the lending facility.
"Today access to the Lombard facility will be further limited as compared to Tuesday," CNB bank board member Ludek Niedermeyer said.
By limiting access to Lombard credit, the central bank squeezes market liquidity and boosts the crown.
Niedermeyer did not elaborate on the limits set by the CNB, but said: "We will react in order to stabilise the currency, so we are willing to cut it (access) to...zero."

The CNB has been waging a war against investors to keep the crown from crashing since last week. Then a wave of short-selling pushed the currency to a record low of more than five percent below the mid-point of the dollar/mark basket, which the central bank uses to fix the crown's exchange rate daily.
"Now the crown is at two percent which is reasonable so it looks like the operations are working, we see mainly stability and maybe some expectations are changing," he added.
Last Friday the CNB raised the Lombard rate from 14 percent to 50 percent in a move bolster the crown, once regarded as the most stable currency in post-communist central Europe.
The CNB also allowed market conditions to determine its repurchase rate, which has since hit 45 percent after 12.9 percent on Friday.
Niedermeyer said the central bank restriction applied equally to all foreign and Czech banks with a licence to operate in the country.

But he added that the policy toward bank branches in the Czech Republic -- which have argued against the move since they are severely limited because their capital is virtually non-existent locally -- had not changed.
"They (branches) were very unhappy but we will not change our policy," he said.
The Czech Republic under economist Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus used to be praised in the West as a model for post-communist reform.
While the CNB has kept inflation in single figures, a soaring current account deficit raised concerns about the Czech economy and the government has slashed earlier forecasts of robust GDP growth.
The crown jumped about 40 basis points against the basket midpoint after the CNB announcement, to around 2.4 percent on the depreciation side of its basket parity in midday trading.
The central bank fixed the crown at 30.359 to the dollar and 17.971 to the mark on Wednesday, implying a deviation against basket parity of - 2.27 percent after a fixing of 2.78 percent on Tuesday.
